t: Minimum Cost to Change the Final Value of Expression — Track (Value, Flip Cost) While Parsing
o: The string is a valid boolean expression over digits 0/1, operators & (AND) and | (OR), and parentheses — with & and | at EQUAL precedence, evaluated strictly left to right inside each parenthesis level. We must report the fewest single-character edits (flip a digit, or swap & with |) needed to make the final value flip. Example 1, "1&(0|1)": the value is 1&1 = 1; changing the | to & gives 1&(0&1) = 0, one edit. Example 2, "(0&0)&(0&0&0)": the value is 0; rewriting it as "(0|1)|(0&0&0)" costs three edits and evaluates to 1, and three is minimal. Example 3, "(0|(1|0&1))": the inner chain evaluates left to right as (1|0)&1 = 1, so the whole value is 1; flipping the inner leading 1 to 0 makes it 0|(0|0&1) = 0 — one edit. With length up to 10^5 we need a linear-time parse rather than any search over edit sequences.
k: Because & and | tie in precedence, a calculator-style stack can collapse eagerly: whenever a new operator or a closing parenthesis arrives, fold all pending fragments at the current bracket level.
For each fragment store two numbers — the minimum edits to force its value to 0 and to force it to 1; a leaf digit costs exactly 1 to flip, and every operator combines only these pairs.
The final value is whichever of the two stored numbers equals 0, so the answer is simply the larger member of the pair computed for the whole expression.

a.i: Mirror the grammar: if the segment is wrapped in redundant outer parentheses, strip them; otherwise split at the LAST top-level operator, so the left piece is exactly what left-to-right evaluation settles first. Solve both sides recursively. To combine, try editing each operand value at most once plus optionally swapping the operator — eight candidate combinations — and keep the cheapest whose truth value differs from the untouched value. Precomputed parenthesis partners keep each split scan linear, but long unparenthesized chains make the recursion quadratic in the worst case.
s: Precompute match[i], the partner index of every parenthesis.
solve(lo, hi): a lone digit returns (value, flipCost = 1); if match[lo] == hi, strip the outer pair and recurse inward.
Otherwise find the LAST top-level operator at index mid and recurse on both halves.
Combine: enumerate {keep or flip left} x {keep or flip right} x {keep or swap operator}; pick the cheapest edit set whose resulting value differs from the original.
Return the pair (value, bestCost); the answer is its cost component.
a.t: O(n^2) worst case — every recursion level rescans its segment (long flat operator chains trigger this); acceptable for moderate inputs but risky at n = 10^5.
a.sp: O(n) — the match array plus recursion depth proportional to parenthesis nesting.

a.n: Approach 2: One-Pass Two Stacks with Closed-Form Folds (Optimal)
a.i: Run a Basic Calculator III style parse: one stack holds (costIfZero, costIfOne) pairs for finished fragments, another holds pending operators and open-parenthesis markers. Whenever an operator or ')' arrives, fold the top two fragments with the top operator. Folding uses closed-form recurrences: for AND, costIfZero = min(zA, zB, 1 + zA + zB) — zero either side, or switch to OR and zero both — and costIfOne = min(oA + oB, 1 + min(oA, oB)) — one both sides, or switch to OR and raise either side. OR swaps the roles of zero and one. After the scan, the single surviving pair describes the whole expression, and the answer is its larger element because the current value corresponds to the member costing 0.
s: Digits push (digit, digit ^ 1) as (costIfZero, costIfOne); '(' pushes a marker onto the operator stack.
On an operator or ')': while the operator-stack top is not the marker, pop two fragments plus an operator and fold; then push the operator or drop the marker.
Fold rule for '&': z = min(zA, zB, 1 + zA + zB), o = min(oA + oB, 1 + min(oA, oB)); for '|' swap the z/o roles.
At the end fold all remaining operators.
Return max(costIfZero, costIfOne) of the final surviving pair.
a.t: O(n) — every character is pushed once and folded at most once.
a.sp: O(n) — both stacks grow with nesting depth and fragment count.

w: Lead with the two-stacks formulation in an interview: equal precedence lets you collapse eagerly, and the (costIfZero, costIfOne) invariant turns the case analysis into mechanical formulas. Verify the recurrences on 0&0 before coding — it needs TWO edits (1&1 or 0|1), which many people get wrong. Pitfalls: forgetting that & does NOT bind tighter than |, splitting divide-and-conquer at the FIRST instead of LAST top-level operator (breaks left-to-right evaluation), and returning the wrong member of the final pair. Follow-ups: minimum edits to reach a specific target value (pick that member of the pair), or reconstructing an edited expression (remember which fold choice achieved each cost).
